full_judgment: 13. We would like to deal with the first question first. Before exercising jurisdiction under any law, either under the Code of Criminal Procedure or the Code of Civil Procedure or under Article 102 of the Constitution or under any other law; be it special or general; the first and the foremost thing, a Court has to see whether the petition/application filed before it is maintainable in law and then whether it has the jurisdiction to give the relief sought in the petition. And we are of the view that the moment, the High Court Division found that the impugned order having been passed by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer as Chairman of the Madrasah, the writ petition was not maintainable, it must have stopped there. The reason of saying so is that article 102 of the Constitution does not authorize the High Court Division exercising special original jurisdiction to pass an order beyond the scope of the writ petition. In the context, we must remind the High Court Division that it does not enjoy the privilege of Article 104 of the Constitution which is enjoyed by this Division only and under the said article this Division can issue any direction, order, decree or writ as may be necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it, including orders for the purpose of securing the attendance of any person or the discovery or production of any document. We conclude by saying that the High Court Division acted in excess of its jurisdiction in declaring the impugned Memo to have been passed without lawful authority and was of no legal effect, after it had found that the writ petition was not maintainable, we would like to add further that a Court of law, be it the writ Court or the Court exercising other jurisdiction cannot give a gratuitous relief or relief in mofte.
